title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page tests whether a natural comparison map is compatible with divided powers. Let F be a functor that can be applied not only to linear maps but also to the non-linear divided-power maps γ^p_X : X → Γ^p(X), x ↦ x^{[p]}. The previous page has Hom(A,M) followed by an arrow u, which suggests F(X) = Hom_set(A,X) or some other functor 'of points' commuting with products, so that F(X) = X^A pointwise.

Grothendieck defines
 u_p : Γ^p F(X) → F(Γ^p X), with u_p(γ^p(x)) = F(γ^p_X)(x).
For F = Hom(A,-) this sends γ^p(φ) to γ^p∘φ. Equivalently, it is the map Γ(M^A) → Γ(M)^A given by the universal property of Γ: the product Γ(M)^A is a PD-algebra and M^A sits in its degree-1 part.

He then draws the square that should commute. Along the top, u_p : Γ^p F(X) → F(Γ^p X), then down by F(η ↦ η^{(q)}) to F(Γ^{pq} X). Along the other side, γ^q : Γ^p F(X) → Γ^{pq} F(X), i.e. ξ ↦ ξ^{(q)}, then u_{pq}. The square is checked on elements γ^p(x):
 F(γ^{q,p}) F(γ^p)(x) = F(γ^{q,p}∘γ^p)(x) = F(α_{pq} γ^{pq})(x) = α_{pq} F(γ^{pq})(x) = α_{pq} u_{pq}(γ^{pq} x) = u_{pq}(γ^q(γ^p x)).
This uses the identity (x^{[p]})^{[q]} = α_{pq} x^{[pq]}, with α_{pq} = (pq)!/((p!)^q q!). It also uses that F is compatible with scalar multiples of maps, which holds for pointwise functors.

The bottom of the page and the next page carry out the standard reduction. To show a ring map of PD-algebras is a PD-morphism, it suffices to check u(x^{(p)}) = u(x)^{(p)} on generators. One then passes to sums via the formula for (Σξ_i)^{(q)}, and to products and monomials via (λ x^{(p)})^{(q)} = λ^q c_{p,q} x^{(pq)} and (ab)^{(q)} = a^q b^{(q)}.

Purpose: to show that ⊕_p Γ^p F(X) → ⊕_p F(Γ^p X) is a morphism of divided-power algebras. This is preparation for the PD de Rham complex and its duality with symmetric algebras (the Ǎ → B̌ duality on the next page). The page is routine bookkeeping in divided-power algebra.
errors: The identity F(αγ) = αF(γ) is used without stating it. It needs F to respect scalar multiplication of (non-linear) maps, which is automatic for pointwise functors such as Hom_set(A,-) but not for an arbitrary functor.
The scrawled line on the next page leaves u_{pq}(γ^q(γ^p x)) = u_{pq}(α_{pq}γ^{pq}x) half-written, but the computation on this page is correct.

ideas.what: Natural comparison map Γ^p F(X) → F(Γ^p X) defined by γ^p(x) ↦ F(γ^p_X)(x)
ideas.modern_name: Canonical map Γ(M^A) → Γ(M)^A; divided powers of a product / functor of points
ideas.where_published: Roby, 'Lois polynômes et lois formelles…'; Berthelot, 'Cohomologie cristalline' (LNM 407)

ideas.what: Compatibility of u with the composition γ^q∘γ^p = α_{pq}γ^{pq}, α_{pq} = (pq)!/((p!)^q q!)
ideas.where_published: Séminaire Cartan; Berthelot–Ogus, Notes on crystalline cohomology

ideas.what: A ring map is a PD-morphism if it commutes with divided powers on generators of the PD-ideal
ideas.where_published: Berthelot LNM 407, Ch. I; Berthelot–Ogus Lemma 3.x

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine verifications of divided-power identities and of PD-morphism compatibility, all standard (Roby, Berthelot). There is nothing new beyond confirming the working method behind the 1976 talk.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'F\Gamma^{\alpha} X' is F(Γ^α X); the subscripts written 'α' in u_α are likely u_p.
'u_p(γ^p_{F(x)}(x)) = F(γ^p_x)(x)': the subscript F(x) under γ indicates divided power taken in F(X). The line reading 'u_α(...) = F(γ^p_x)' is the same formula with '(x)' omitted.
Left vertical arrow label is 'ξ ↦ ξ^{(q)}' (not γ^{(q)}); right arrow is F(η ↦ η^{(q)}).
The struck line '[-x↦-] F(X) →^1 FΓ^p(x)' is a crossed-out attempt; '[-#-]' is a struck symbol.
'λ = p' at the bottom is probably 'λ ∈ ...' or a struck fragment, not an equation.
